champion: Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block
ordered_diagnoses: Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block

facts.raw_span: A patient in their 70s
medical history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension
presented to the emergency department with fatigue, light-headedness, and dyspnea on exertion during the previous week
heart rate of 47 beats per minute
blood pressure of 148/59 mm Hg
Normal sinus rhythm at 72 beats per minute
PR interval prolongs between first and second conducted beats
Some P waves do not conduct to ventricles
Right bundle-branch block present
Prolonged His-ventricular (HV) interval of 75 milliseconds on first conducted beat, extending to 277 milliseconds on second conducted beat
Normal biventricular function without significant valvular lesions
Surface ECG showed sinus rhythm

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with fatigue, light-headedness, and dyspnea on exertion, combined with ECG findings of normal sinus rhythm at 72 beats per minute, PR interval prolongation, and some P waves not conducting to ventricles, suggests Sick Sinus Syndrome.

concepts.preferred_label: Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block
concepts.why: The ECG findings of PR interval prolongation between first and second conducted beats, some P waves not conducting to ventricles, and a prolonged His-ventricular interval, are consistent with Mobitz Type II Second-Degree Atrioventricular Block.
The presence of a Right Bundle Branch Block, as indicated by the ECG findings, suggests this diagnosis.
The combination of ECG findings, including PR interval prolongation, some P waves not conducting to ventricles, and a prolonged His-ventricular interval, suggests a Cardiac Conduction Disease.
The ECG findings of PR interval prolongation, some P waves not conducting to ventricles, and a prolonged His-ventricular interval, are consistent with an Atrioventricular Block.

rationales.F07: PR interval prolongation is a sign of first-degree AV block, which can be seen in Mobitz Type II
rationales.F08: Non-conducted P waves are a hallmark of Mobitz Type II second-degree AV block
rationales.F09: Right bundle-branch block is a specific finding for C03
rationales.F10: Prolonged His-ventricular interval is a sign of cardiac conduction disease, specifically affecting the AV node
